# TUI key reference

Press `?` in the TUI to read this sheet on screen; the surface you are
on is the first section there. Every footer row names `?:help` where the
key answers. In a chat, `?` opens the sheet only while the draft is
empty -- once a sentence has started it is an ordinary question mark.
The command palette is `:`.

## Global

| Keys | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Tab / Shift-Tab` | next / previous surface |
| `3` | jump to Keepers when the active field or panel does not use 3 |
| `r` | refresh the current surface |
| `i` | focus the composer; on Dashboard, choose a Keeper |
| `:` | command palette |
| `;` | agenda: what is coming, and who is waiting on you; Enter opens a row |
| `@` | answering: who is mid-turn or just finished; Enter opens their chat |
| `?` | this help |
| `&` | Collab: watch MSX/DOS and manage play links (also `:` go Collab) |
| `Ctrl-B` | show or hide the Keeper roster; it starts hidden and the choice persists across navigation and resizing |
| `Ctrl-L` | cycle the Activity pane narrow, wide or hidden; the wheel over the pane scrolls the full list; a press picks a keeper, a second press opens its chat; /activity order turns the order of its calls, /activity scroll moves the pane |
| `Ctrl-W` | focus the Activity pane: a cursor lands on its first row, j/k walk the rows a press acts on and scroll past the last, Enter opens or closes the call under it, Esc or Ctrl-W gives the keys back; the chat keeps Ctrl-W for its draft until the draft is empty |
| `Ctrl-^` | show or hide Browser Lane; retain tab and scroll |
| `Ctrl-T` | the mouse starts with masc: a drag selects inside the pane it began in (Keeper roster, surface or Activity pane) and copies it on release via OSC 52, a press that does not move clicks, and Esc drops a selection still held; Ctrl-T hands the mouse to the terminal for its own selection across the whole window, and Ctrl-T again takes it back |
| `Ctrl-]` | follow the reference under the cursor; Esc on the surface it opens comes back here |
| `q` | quit |

Keeper settings `e` reads a fresh snapshot asynchronously before opening the
external editor. After the editor returns, workspace rechecking and the guarded
save also run asynchronously; navigation stays available while the receipt is
pending. Repeated `e` shares that pending save. The footer retains progress or
failure for the selected Keeper, and a late receipt cannot refresh another Keeper.

After a refusal or unconfirmed result, `e` reads current settings and restores
only your changed values for review in the editor. Untouched fields use current
values. The old revision and context-shrink confirmation are not reused; saving
requires the new editor roundtrip. Original input and receipts stay with their
operation. Sandbox shortcuts use the same owned save operation: they read current
settings and the required revision before sending the selected profile. Repeated
keys share a pending same-Keeper save; selecting a new profile never rewrites it.
An already observed matching profile sends no POST. Failed shortcuts retain their
selection; an explicit next key rereads current before another save. Retained editor
changes survive shortcut operations. The external editor keeps its own terminal
interaction. Runtime and painted latency remain unmeasured.

Keeper Runtime picker assignments also retain an owned operation: original
Keeper, workspace, concrete Runtime or clear-to-default choice, current snapshot,
and assignment revision. Navigation stays available; a pending same-Keeper
Settings, Sandbox or assignment save prevents another dispatch without closing
the picker. Different Keepers retain independent operations. The existing config
read and assignment POST remain the two logical save requests. Local workspace
and read authority are checked again before POST; server assignment CAS remains
the write precondition. This adds no atomic server workspace precondition.

Progress, warnings, conflicts and uncertain outcomes stay with the original
operation for this TUI session. Cancellation before possible dispatch is not-sent;
after possible dispatch it is unconfirmed. HTTP 400 can include an IO failure,
so it does not prove that no write happened. Explicitly choosing again reads
current revision; the old request never resends itself. A committed receipt proves
configured assignment and the application results it reports, not which Runtime
is executing a current Keeper turn. Execution and painted latency remain unmeasured.

Runtime catalogue consumers share an in-flight catalogue read for the same
workspace. Explicit refresh and post-save demand wait for one fresh follow-up
after that read, rather than starting overlapping catalogue requests. Further
refreshes during the follow-up may require another read. Last observed rows stay
visible with refreshing/stale status and the latest refresh failure. A successful
empty response completes the read; it does not keep saying loading. Exact slot
replacement still waits for a fresh catalogue. Nested pickers and recent-context
catalogue demand resume after workspace reconfirmation. A different workspace
clears the old rows and demand. This sharing covers the catalogue launcher;
Overview and the Runtime operator surface retain their separate readers.
Catalogue rows, configured default route and Keeper assignments share one
validated observation. A missing usage-window observation stays an explicit
unknown alongside an otherwise usable catalogue.
Overview keeps catalogue and usage availability independent: valid usage remains
available after catalogue validation fails, and usage failure leaves healthy
catalogue rows usable. Both observations belong to the same response; a failed
usage read does not borrow a prior response's quota identity.
Full-refresh progress labels a composed read as partial when one returned result
failed, naming both failed and received components. This covers Runtime
catalogue/usage, Board posts/hearths and available Keeper roster/Candle results.
Partial is separate from full receipt; unfinished logical readers remain interrupted when
the refresh stops. These notices do not grant action authority or confirm Task completion.
Board also reports its posts/hearth readers before the pair returns. A completed
child remains visible when its parent fails or stops. A caught child cancellation
is interrupted; a started child without a terminal observation is unfinished.
Child intervals describe those observations, not proven worker exit or screen paint.
Board posts and hearth data also arrive independently under their original request.
Ready posts do not wait for the census; a pending or failed census retains its
last successful value. One dataset does not consume its sibling's result, and a
terminal bundle does not replay early data. Board remains pending while either
dataset is outstanding. These are UI-state rules; actual paint latency is unmeasured.
Census now distinguishes not read, initial reading, received (including empty),
unavailable and a retained observation after failure. Refreshing/stale values stay
available for hearth navigation; the census row and palette identify them as last
observed. Header/sidebar totals use only a received census without a pending census
read. A collector ending without a census result records unavailability. Workspace
withdrawal clears census values and candidates along with other Board data.
The post list has its own typed observation and pending slot. Initial loading,
not read, received empty and failed are distinct. Refresh/failure retains posts,
selected identity and compose input; list/sidebar and palette qualify retained
posts as last observed. A detail response enriches one matching row while keeping
the list's failure and pending ownership. Missing terminal results remain
unavailable, and workspace withdrawal clears list candidates. Changing sort/hearth
keeps the old listing with its original query until a new one succeeds, even if the
old result was empty. The listing/sidebar and palette qualify that observation;
its sort explanation, age column and census total use the observed query. Requested
controls stay separate, and detail enrichment does not relabel the list.
Admission diagnostics additionally keep the response's query, the controls at
application and the retained listing's query separate for success/failure. Missing
owned terminal data has no invented response query. These are request-linked log
fields; actual runtime logs and visible behavior remain separate evidence.
Full/navigation dispatch diagnostics also retain the original and current source
request through cold identity handoff. Planned Board conditions stay fixed even
if controls move; an originally non-Board read stays unrequested in that context.
Dispatch/rebind/cleanup observations are separate from actual HTTP starts, received
data and paint. A missing finish record remains an unfinished observation.

Runtime model and account form saves keep input and its opening revision while
workspace checks, source reading, preview and guarded commit run outside the
key handler. Repeated submission shares the pending operation. During a pending
save, Esc leaves the form and keeps its operation; reopening Models with e/c or
runtime.toml with a restores the original input. A disconnected commit remains
unconfirmed and cannot be submitted again from that retained form. Ctrl-X closes
a retained terminal form and rereads configuration; the next open starts fresh.
The original receipt stays in session history. Confirmed account saves retain
their sign-in command in the session log. File commit, durability and runtime
application remain separate facts. Runtime and painted input latency are unmeasured.

The runtime.toml editor also returns to the input loop before its save finishes;
S retries a retained draft through the same owned asynchronous save. Its original
path, source revision and complete edited text are submitted together. Repeated
saves wait for the existing operation. Navigation keeps the draft; a late receipt
can complete only its original editing intent, including after ordinary source
refreshes, and cannot delete a later edit with the same text.

After an unconfirmed commit or durability result, older comparisons and already
in-flight reads cannot authorize retry. Read current with r, then explicitly use
u to keep your text and choose that revision, or U to replace the text. Choosing
a new base from a pre-outcome reading also cannot bypass revalidation. X discards
only the local draft; it does not claim that a pending server write was cancelled.
These changes do not make the external editor itself asynchronous or establish
measured key/paint latency.

Config source observations prepare whole-source tokenization, terminal sanitization
and the model table together from one immutable reading before UI admission.
Preparation uses the shared CPU path: the model table consumes already interpreted
server declarations instead of reparsing Runtime source or expanding local credential
homes. It reads no UI, environment, request ownership or palette state. The server
model envelope must match the reading's exact path and revision. Missing, unavailable
or malformed model evidence stays failed; source and other observations remain usable.
Source-only form parsing still retains Runtime's environment effects.
Account-group/model interpretation failure leaves the source available; email
observation failure stays independent. Model selection and source revision come
from that same reading.

Ordinary refreshes reuse an unchanged retained draft's existing tokenization and
the matching observation's current-file projection. Sharing tokenization does
not share editing ownership, adopt a revision or authorize retry. Existing
workspace/read authority, generation checks and queued follow-up policy still
control admission. Diagnostic clocks distinguish request start, prepared result
and UI admission decision; these are not painted-frame or key-latency evidence.

When a selected question is too tall for the compact Approvals panel, it keeps
a short preview from the original question instead of disappearing behind a
hidden-question count. Where space permits, the preview points to `a` for the
complete Ask and its answers. The preview does not select or submit an answer;
the existing answer reader keeps the full prompt, choices and draft. With only
one content row, the selected preview takes that row; with none, no extra hidden
count is drawn beyond the available space.

## System / Tools

| Keys | What it does |
|---|---|
| `j/k` | scroll |
| `PgUp/PgDn` | page |
| `Home/End` | top/bottom |
| `p` | available / async runs / receipts / usage / all tools |
| `J/K` | in async runs, select an original request; otherwise select a published Skill |
| `[ / ]` | change the effective Keeper surface |
| `c / C` | open $EDITOR on a template for a new Skill; c starts an instruction Skill, C starts a composition Skill |
| `e` | open the selected SKILL.md in $EDITOR, validate, CAS-save, and publish |
| `Esc` | return from original Task to request, then request to list; otherwise back to the System surface it hangs off |
| `r` | refresh the open original Task body/history, original request detail, or Tools list |
| `Enter` | in async runs, read the selected original request |
| `t / T` | from async request detail, read its original source Task and history |
| `H` | from original Task detail, read earlier stored history; retains the observed prefix on failure |
| `o / O` | in async runs, edit the original submitter, request ID and target Keeper for an exact lookup |

Work Task detail and Tools original Task detail use source-bound history pages.
`H` extends the captured prefix; a failed page retains the same cursor for an
explicit retry. `r` requests a fresh latest prefix while keeping the prior
observation visible. The page demand follows terminal height, with no total
history cap. Exhaustion means the observed stored prefix ended; retained-away
history and Task completion are separate facts. Tools cadence does not reset a
paged history. A source change can refuse the cursor; use `r` to read anew.

Task body and history prepare independently. Their notices distinguish waiting
to start, arranging the text, waiting for the prepared result, and waiting for
the display state to update. An earlier display stays labelled while a newer
one is prepared. These stages describe display preparation, not Task progress
or completion.

## Chat marks

| Keys | What it does |
|---|---|
| `◌ running` | arguments still arriving |
| `▶ awaiting result` | arguments sent, result not back yet |
| `✓ returned` | result came back |
| `◌ native running` | native step running |
| `■ native ended` | native step ended; provider report shown when available, not a MASC execution receipt |
| `✗ native failed` | provider reported an error, a decline or a nonzero exit for its native step; not a MASC execution receipt |
| `✗ failed` | the tool answered with a failure |
| `○ result not seen` | no result was seen in this view before the attempt ended; this does not establish that the tool failed |
| `? outcome unrecorded` | the stored record has no outcome field; a gap in the record, not a failure |
| `↩ received` | a result is present; receipt alone does not establish success |
| `읽는 중` | the model asked to read the skill; nothing back yet |
| `읽음, 전달 확인 중` | the skill text came back; the server's delivery record is not read yet |
| `읽음, 전달 기록 없음` | the skill text came back; the server has no record of delivering it |
| `전달됨, 도구 안 씀` | the server recorded the delivery; no tool call followed from it |
| `전달됨, 도구 씀` | the server recorded the delivery and the tool calls the model made because of it (the rows marked observed action) |
| `실패` | reading the skill failed |
| `결과 못 봄` | this pane never saw the read come back; says nothing about the skill |
| `기록 형식 안 맞음` | the server's skill record is in a shape this build cannot read |
| `실행 중` | as above, for a composition: the skill ran as its own tool rather than being read as text |
| `실행됨, 전달 확인 중` | as above, for a composition: the skill ran as its own tool rather than being read as text |
| `실행됨, 전달 기록 없음` | as above, for a composition: the skill ran as its own tool rather than being read as text |
| `proof` | the ids behind a skill row: use= the read call, turn= the turn, runtime= who ran it, rev= the skill text's revision |
| `observed action` | a tool call the server attributes to the skill above it |
